title: Jesa by Jeena Yi at The Public #jesa #thepublictheater #mayitheaterco...
transcript: When four Korean American sisters come together to honor their late parents with a traditional Jesa ceremony, it's anything but a perfect family gathering. To start, the sisters are very different and they each have their own baggage and resentments. Old conflicts surface, and the night reaches a fever pitch that's practically supernatural. The premise here is interesting and the relationships feel believable — It's funny how they spew such vile insults at each other and then just move on nonchalantly, as so many siblings do. Pretty much any critiques I have stem from its run time. Despite only being 90 minutes long, it runs out of steam. The acting begins to feel one-dimensional because there's only so much you can excavate from these characters in such a contained scene. The play also moves at a naturally modest speed the entire time, so it can only keep your attention for so long. But if you enjoy stories of sisterhood or a good old family drama, Jesa is running now at the public. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
